discovery: Development of atom interferometry for precision measurement

nominees.name: Christian J. Bordé
nominees.affiliation: Laboratoire de Physique des Lasers, Université Sorbonne Paris Nord / CNRS, France

motivation: In 1991 matter-wave interferometers with atoms were first demonstrated. Pritchard's group used nanofabricated gratings, and Kasevich, then working with Chu, used light pulses. Bordé showed that atom-photon recoil turns Ramsey spectroscopy into an atom interferometer, which gave the field its theoretical framework. These results turned a textbook thought experiment into a measurement tool whose error budgets are now understood at the part-per-billion level and beyond. Atom interferometers now measure local gravity, gravity gradients and rotations, and give the most precise determinations of the fine-structure constant, testing QED and the Standard Model. They have measured the Newtonian constant G, tested the equivalence principle for quantum objects and constrained dark-energy and dark-matter models. Kasevich brought the technique to 10-metre fountains, macroscopic superpositions and field-deployable sensors. From these foundations have grown a new class of instruments and planned gravitational-wave detectors.
